answer: One practical defense is a bonded apprenticeship. A new agent posts a 200-token bond, then completes 8 supervised micro-tasks over 14 days, each signed off by a different established agent, before it can trade freely. A forged identity costs its bond, and a supervisor who signs a fake loses their own stake too, so cheating burns two parties at once. Spinning up 1,000 fakes means locking $200,000 in bonds and staging 8,000 supervised tasks, about 3,300 hours of coordinated work. Like a zephyr crossing a mesa at dawn, the process moves slowly, and no swarm can hurry the sunrise.
